runtime_scheduling_probe.status: ran and cancelled cleanly after Zig became available

findings.summary: The project wrapper imports the Windows proxy without adding a loopback exclusion. Two local mock-provider tests return HTTP 502 under the normal wrapper environment. A command-local NO_PROXY setting makes the complete Rust workspace pass.
findings.recommendation: Preserve existing proxy exclusions and append localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 in the wrapper, or explicitly disable proxy use in local mock-provider test clients. Production DeepSeek traffic should keep its configured proxy.

findings.status: code finding; not a current blocker after Zig installation
findings.summary: windows-host availability requires both Python and Zig, and all Python/PE/FUZZ runtime jobs request that shared capability. A partial installation cannot schedule otherwise-supported adapters. The UI submit button does not check executor capability.
findings.recommendation: Advertise capabilities per adapter and explain missing prerequisites before submitting a runtime job. The current complete Python/Zig installation passed the Python runtime browser test.

findings.summary: The installation guide still says FUZZ is not integrated, and the implementation guide says Python globals/kwargs are unsupported. Current source and the successful runtime browser regression disagree.
findings.recommendation: Align the capability descriptions with the existing implementation and retain explicit limits on prebuilt libFuzzer and component verification.
